title: Because it was he
hook: Montaigne on his friend La Boétie: because it was he, because it was I (Essays 1.28)

segments.voice: Yesterday's word was another self, Aristotle's allos autos. Your line was isn't at war inside. Today, his careful lists meet a friendship that wouldn't fit on any list.

Two men in France have heard about each other for a while, and each is curious about the other. Then, by chance, they meet at a great feast, in the middle of a crowd. By the end of that first meeting, one of them later wrote, they were so taken with each other that nothing was ever again as close to either of them as the other. The writer was Michel de Montaigne. The friend was Étienne de La Boétie. The essay is called, simply, Of Friendship.
screen: `A FEAST AND A CROWD.` → `MONTAIGNE AND LA BOÉTIE.`

segments.voice: First, the question he can't answer. If someone pressed him to say why he loved his friend, Montaigne says, he could only answer: because it was he, because it was I. No list of reasons, no virtues counted up. Second, the seam disappears. In this friendship, the two souls were so mingled that the seam joining them couldn't be found. He sets it apart from what he calls common friendships, where you walk with the bridle in your hand, with prudence and caution. In theirs, everything was held in common, so neither could even be said to give the other anything. Third, cut short. La Boétie died, and the friendship ended far sooner than Montaigne wanted. Set beside the time he had with his friend, he writes, the rest of his life was smoke, a long dark night. Fourth, against the list. Two days ago Aristotle explained friendship by what it rests on, and yesterday by its marks. Montaigne doesn't throw that out. But he insists a friendship like this can't be fully explained from the outside. You can describe it; you can't give its reasons. The reason is the person, two names and nothing else.
screen: `THE QUESTION HE CAN'T ANSWER.` · `THE SEAM DISAPPEARS.` · `CUT SHORT.` · `AGAINST THE LIST.` · then, large: `BECAUSE IT WAS HE.`

segments.voice: Let your deepest friendship come to mind, whether it's going on now, or faded, or lost to death, and don't explain it: just let their face, their voice, something they used to say be there. If reasons arrive, let them pass by, and rest in the plain fact of them. If no friendship like that comes, let the one you'd hope for sit there instead, without a face yet.
Montaigne, who said he loved his friend because it was he, because it was I, with no list of reasons to give. Today's word.
Your line: smoke, a long dark night. That is how the years felt without his friend. Day eight hundred twenty-four, done.

howItsDone: Montaigne's essay Of Friendship, from the first book of his Essays, is read in literature and philosophy courses, and some readers turn to it when they're grieving a friend.

notes: Montaigne paraphrased throughout (Florio 1603 and Cotton 1685 are public domain but not on the validator's list); the title phrase follows the index.
In perfect friendship all things are common, so there is no lending or giving between the friends: paraphrased from the same essay; confirm.
Chapter numbering differs by edition (1.27 in some, 1.28 in others); confirm.

Often noted by scholars: the second clause, 'parce que c'était moi', was added later in Montaigne's hand in the Bordeaux copy. Left out of the script under the claims rule; a scholar may want it as a trapdoor detail.
'Smoke, a long dark night' paraphrases Montaigne's description of his life after La Boétie's death; confirm. La Boétie's age at death and the length of the friendship are deliberately not stated.
French in the original game: confirm spelling and the pronunciation guide.
Editor: removed the claim that Montaigne says the seam can still be found in ordinary friendships (he says only that in this one it could not be found); teach and trapdoor reworded.

Audit: 'common friendships, which he also kept, more carefully' was garbled and not quite what the essay says; replaced with Montaigne's own image, paraphrased: in common friendships one walks bridle in hand, with prudence and caution. Meeting at a great feast after hearing of each other, the seam, all things in common and 'smoke, a dark night' checked against the essay.
